what_its_for: Valproate is used to treat seizures (epilepsy), bipolar disorder (mood swings including mania), and to prevent migraine headaches. Your doctor may also use it for other conditions not listed here.
how_to_take: Take valproate exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow tablets and capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them unless your doctor says it is okay. The sprinkle capsules can be opened and the contents sprinkled onto a small amount of soft food like applesauce, then swallowed right away without chewing. Take with food or milk if the medicine upsets your stomach. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this could cause serious problems like increased seizures.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your condition, weight, and how your body responds to the medicine. Most adults start with a low dose that is slowly increased. Take it at the same time(s) each day to keep a steady level in your body. Never take more than your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store valproate at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking valproate — it can increase drowsiness and the risk of liver problems. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires full alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking aspirin, blood thinners, or other seizure medications without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as these can interact with valproate. Women of childbearing age: avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine unless you have discussed it with your doctor, as it can cause serious birth defects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: unusual bleeding or bruising, severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), sudden severe headache, confusion or unusual behavior changes, thoughts of hurting yourself, extreme tiredness or weakness, swelling of the face or body, loss of seizure control, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, or trouble breathing. These could be signs of serious side effects including liver damage or a life-threatening condition called pancreatitis.
when_it_works: You may not feel the full benefit of valproate right away. For seizures and bipolar disorder, it may take several days to a few weeks to reach the right level in your blood. For migraine prevention, it may take up to 4 to 6 weeks to notice improvement. Keep taking it even if you feel well — stopping suddenly can cause your condition to get worse.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Valproate can cause serious birth defects, especially to the baby's brain and spine, and should NOT be used during pregnancy if possible. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor immediately about safer options. WOMEN OF CHILDBEARING AGE: Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and discuss this with your doctor. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of valproate, especially drowsiness, and may need a lower dose. CHILDREN: Dosing is based on weight and is carefully managed by the doctor. Children under 2 years old have a higher risk of serious liver problems. LIVER OR KIDNEY DISEASE: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney problems, as this medicine may not be safe for you or may require a dose adjustment.
